summary: Planned in 1940 and built in 1948 as a 100-foot Aermotor tower at Piper's Corner, Burlington County; still in service, with a staffed observer described in 2026.

facts.design: 100-foot Aermotor tower with a 7x7-foot metal cab

access.note: Working NJFFS observation post; a 2026 WHYY report describes a staffed observer on duty, and no source read describes public climbing.

events.note: Plans for the tower were set in 1940, per the NHLR page
Construction in 1948 after World War II; 1948 newspaper says it was being erected by Corlen Engineering Co. of Collingswood for about $4,500

evidence.quote: Plans for the Medford Station Fire Tower were set in 1940, but construction was not accomplished until 1948 after World War II.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: WHYY describes the tower as above Wharton State Forest, while the register and the Division B page give Piper's Corner, Burlington County. The story uses Piper's Corner; the wording differs but the sources do not directly contradict each other.

notes_for_editor: Strongest of the three: the 1940 plans, 1948 construction, 2004 registration and 2026 staffing description agree across sources. The builder and cost come from a single 1948 newspaper item reprinted on the Forest Lookouts page; the register does not name a builder. The WHYY article (updated June 9, 2026) is the only current staffing source. The register's photo is marked All rights reserved and was not reused. The NJ DEP fire-towers page returned no text, so it was not used.
